rows.en: I spread out my lunch alone.

ghs.en: Alone, I unfolded and spreaded out my packed lunch.
ghs.assessment: The past tense of 'spread' is 'spread,' not 'spreaded.'

rows.jp: あいかわらず二人分の弁当だった。
rows.en: As ever, it was a lunch for two.

ghs.en: Packed lunch was enough for two, as usual.

rows.jp: やることもなく、再び屋上に。
rows.en: Nothing else to do. Back to the roof.

ghs.en: With not a thing to do, I go again to the rooftop.

rows.jp: フェンスから外界を見渡している。
rows.en: She was looking out through the fence at the world beyond.

ghs.en: taking in the view of the outside world from the fence.

rows.jp: 既視感が、俺の意識を過去昔へと連れ去った。
rows.en: Déjà vu carried my consciousness away into the distant past.

ghs.en: Paramnesia kidnapped my awareness to the distant past.
ghs.assessment: 既視感 is a sense of déjà vu. 'Paramnesia' is a broader clinical term, and awareness is not idiomatically 'kidnapped' into memory.

rows.jp: 夏も終わりかけていた。

ghs.en: Summer was also in its ending,
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says summer was drawing to an end. 'In its ending' is not idiomatic English.

highlights.text: Summer was also in its ending

rows.jp: 蝉たちも一際うるさかった。
rows.en: The cicadas, too, were especially loud.

rows.jp: 叩きつけるような鳴き声。

ghs.en: Cries loud like slaps in the face.

rows.jp: 最後の命を振り絞っていると知れる。
rows.en: You could hear them wringing out the last of their lives.

ghs.en: Straining their voice to make it known that they are summoning the last of their life force.
ghs.assessment: The narrator can tell that the cicadas are wringing out the last of their lives. The English turns this inference into the cicadas' purpose and changes expending their remaining life into summoning a life force.

highlights.text: to make it known that they are summoning the last of their life force

rows.jp: 命の残滓に彩られる夏。
rows.en: Summer, painted with the residue of life.

ghs.en: It was a Summer tinged in the dregs of life.

rows.jp: 背後からでも、肩の震えを見ればわかる。
rows.en: Even from behind, I could tell by the trembling of her shoulders.

ghs.en: Even from the back, that shaking of the shoulders is unmistakable.

ghs.assessment: The Japanese school-status address is left as an unexplained honorific rather than represented in English.

rows.en: She made no attempt to hide her tears.

ghs.en: She does not hide her tears.
Kiri: "Yutaka... Yutaka, he... fell from here..."

ghs.assessment: The first-person narrator says that he knew. The English changes the subject to Kiri.

rows.jp: 知らない者はいなかった。

ghs.en: There was no one who didn't,

rows.jp: 世間一般では、学生が一人飛び降り自殺をすれば、それなりに話題になる。
rows.en: Ordinarily, when a student jumps to their death, it causes something of a stir.

ghs.en: In society at large, a student leaping off to his death on his own would be newsworthy, in some way.

rows.jp: 保護者は学校を問いつめ、誰が悪いのか、白日のもとにさらそうとする。
rows.en: Parents press the school for answers, trying to drag whoever is responsible into the light of day.

ghs.en: Guardians would press the school with questions, so as to bring to daylight who was in the wrong.

rows.jp: 学校も責任を回避しようとする。
rows.en: The school, in turn, tries to evade responsibility.

ghs.en: And the school, then, would try to avoid responsibility.

rows.en: None of that happened at Gunjo.

ghs.en: But at Gunjou there is none of that.

rows.jp: 世間の誰も問いつめてはこないし、学校も逃げない。
rows.en: No one from the outside came demanding answers, and the school did not shirk.

ghs.en: No one in society would press questions, and the school would not dodge them.

rows.jp: 何人かの人間が責任を取った。
世間は群青の危険な少年少女たちのことなど、どうでも良かった。
rows.en: The world did not care what happened to Gunjo's dangerous boys and girls.

ghs.en: To the world, the dangerous boys and girls of Gunjou and all that is around them could do whatever they wanted with themselves.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the wider world did not care about Gunjou's dangerous boys and girls. The English instead says the students and their surroundings could do whatever they wanted with themselves.

highlights.text: To the world, the dangerous boys and girls of Gunjou and all that is around them could do whatever they wanted with themselves.

rows.jp: 「誰も……誰も……悲しまない……わたしたちがどういう気持ちで……生きてきたのか……誰もっ」
rows.en: “No one... no one is grieving... No one cares how we felt... how we've lived... No one!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "No one... no one... is even sad... for all the feelings that we had lived with... no one!"
There was a rare excitement here.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says Kiri was unusually agitated. The English removes her as subject and turns her state into an unidentified excitement in a place.

highlights.text: There was a rare excitement here.

rows.jp: 豊の死から、すでに一週間が経過していた。
rows.en: A full week had already passed since Yutaka's death.

ghs.en: One week had already passed since Yutaka's death.

rows.jp: 霧の悲嘆は遅れてきていた。

ghs.en: Kiri's grief had come behind schedule.

rows.jp: 「なあ霧……豊は、幸せだったのかな」
rows.en: “Kiri... do you think Yutaka was happy?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Say, Kiri, I'm wondering... was Yutaka happy?"

rows.jp: 「あいつはあいつなりに、幸せだったのかな？」
rows.en: “Do you think he was happy in his own way?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm wondering, was that guy happy, even in his own way?"

ghs.assessment: 'Usual' begins with a consonant sound and takes 'a,' not 'an.'

rows.jp: 意味はまったく逆だった。

ghs.en: the meaning was wholly and damnably the opposite.

rows.jp: 「……ずっと、つらい思いをしてきたんです」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...always, he was always feeling bitter."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says Yutaka had been suffering or enduring painful experiences. 'Feeling bitter' instead suggests resentment.
The question asks whether it was truly painful or hard the entire time. 'Bitter' changes suffering into resentment.

rows.jp: 「一瞬でも、幸せな時間はなかった？」
rows.en: “Wasn't there even one moment when he was happy?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "There were never times of happiness, not even one instant?"

rows.jp: 「……先輩と友達になってからは……笑うように……」
rows.en: “...After he became friends with you... he started to smile...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...since he became friends with you, Senpai... he seemed to be smiling..."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese address is left as an unexplained honorific, and 笑うように means he began or came to smile after becoming friends with Taichi, not merely that he seemed to be smiling.

highlights.text: you, Senpai... he seemed to be smiling

rows.jp: 「けど全然取り戻してないっ」
rows.en: “But he never got any of it back!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "But he did not recover in the slightest!"

rows.jp: 「受けた苦しみを、ちっとも取り戻してないっ」
rows.en: “It didn't come close to making up for all the suffering he endured!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "He didn't recover at all, not from all the anguish he had suffered!"
ghs.assessment: Kiri says that none of the suffering inflicted on him had been made up for or restored to him. The English instead says that he personally failed to recover from anguish.

highlights.text: He didn't recover at all, not from all the anguish he had suffered!

rows.jp: 「じゃあ霧ちんは、豊の人生が取るに足らないものだったと思ってるわけか」
rows.en: “So you think Yutaka's life amounted to nothing, Kiri-kins?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Therefore, Kiri-chin, you think that the life Yutaka was living had no value, do you?"
ghs.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address is left unexplained rather than represented in English.

rows.jp: 「……と言ってはみたものの、悲しいのは理屈じゃないものな」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...so I might say, however, sadness is not something rational."
ghs.assessment: と言ってはみたものの means 'that said' or 'although I say that.' The English sequence does not form the intended concessive relation idiomatically.
迷っていた means Taichi was uncertain or conflicted over what to do with Kiri, not that he failed to understand something.

rows.en: About what should be done with Kiri.

ghs.en: as to how to treat Kiri.

rows.en: I looked up at the sky.

ghs.en: I look up at the sky.

rows.jp: 視界を埋めた純白が、巨大な入道雲と理解できるまでの刹那。
rows.en: For an instant, pure white filled my vision before resolving into a vast thunderhead.

ghs.en: An instant passed before I could understand that the pure white my vision was buried in was an enormous cluster of cumulonimbus.
ghs.assessment: 入道雲 refers to one enormous towering cumulonimbus cloud. 'Cumulonimbus' is being used as a mass/category noun after 'cluster of' rather than naming that cloud.

rows.jp: 蝉たちの最期とともに。
rows.en: Along with the cicadas' final hours.

ghs.en: Along with the last moments of the cicadas' lives.

rows.jp: 万感こもごも含んだ意味に、霧には聞こえたのだろう。
rows.en: Kiri must have heard all the tangled emotion in those words.

ghs.en: Kiri must have heard thousands of feelings within that meaning, one after the other.
ghs.assessment: 万感こもごも means the words carried a whole mixture or flood of emotions. The English literalizes 万 as an exact count and turns simultaneous mixed feeling into a temporal sequence.

highlights.text: thousands of feelings within that meaning, one after the other

rows.jp: 「……うわぁぁぁぁぁぁぁぁぁぁぁぁぁ！」
目を伏せ、俺のシャツの裾を掴んで、声を張り上げた。
rows.en: She lowered her eyes, seized the hem of my shirt, and wailed.

ghs.en: Eyes downcast, grabbing the hem of my shirt, and screaming out.

rows.jp: 「ゆたにぃが……死んじゃった……死んで……」

ghs.assessment: Kiri's intimate childish form for her older brother is left as an unexplained Japanese suffix construction.
嗚咽 means sobbing. Tears do not themselves wail, and the English changes the physical action into an abstract sound.
The intimate older-brother address is reproduced in Japanese morphology without an English representation.

rows.jp: 大好きな、お兄ちゃんだったわけだ。
rows.en: The big brother she had loved so dearly.

ghs.en: He was her beloved onii-chan, that's what he was.
ghs.assessment: お兄ちゃん identifies her beloved older brother in an affectionate register. The English leaves the kinship term and suffix untranslated.

rows.jp: 片足でも立派に生きて。
rows.en: He had lived admirably, even with one leg.

ghs.en: Living magnificently even if on one leg.

rows.jp: 豊の葬式で見た二人の顔には、軽い安堵があった。
rows.en: The faces I saw at Yutaka’s funeral held a trace of relief.

ghs.en: The face I saw on those two at Yutaka's funeral was that of faint relief.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese refers to the expressions on both parents' faces. The English combines plural 'those two' with one face.

highlights.text: The face I saw on those two

rows.jp: 霧はそのことに気づいているのか。
おそらく、悟っているに違いなかった。

ghs.en: I believe that she did realize that, and no mistake.

rows.jp: いろんなつらい目に遭っても、二人で支え合ってきたんだろう。
rows.en: However much they suffered, the two of them must have supported each other.

ghs.en: Whatever hardship their eyes met, the two would have supported each other.
ghs.assessment: つらい目に遭う is an idiom meaning to undergo hardships. The English incorrectly makes their literal eyes encounter hardship.

rows.en: He had been her other half.

ghs.en: Kiri is only an half, yes.
ghs.assessment: 'Half' begins with a consonant sound and takes 'a,' not 'an.'

rows.jp: ただ霧は、望んでそうなった。
rows.en: Only Kiri had chosen to become that way.

ghs.en: Except Kiri seemed to have wished for that.
ghs.assessment: 望んでそうなった says that Kiri became that way because she wanted or chose it. The English misreads そうなった as evidential 'seemed' and reduces the deliberate result to a past wish.

highlights.text: seemed to have wished for that

rows.jp: 今は強い感情が気力を剥奪している。
rows.en: For now, powerful emotion had stripped away her strength.

ghs.en: Right now, strong emotions are depriving her of vigor.

rows.jp: が、いずれ悲しみが薄れれば、あるべきはずのもう半分を求めるだろう。
rows.en: But once her grief faded, she would seek the other half that ought to have been there.

ghs.en: But should someday the sadness grow faint, she will be searching for that half that she expects to be there, that must be there.
ghs.assessment: The inverted conditional places 'someday' between the modal and subject in a non-English order.

highlights.text: should someday the sadness grow faint

rows.en: Two people who had been one body and soul.

ghs.assessment: 一心同体 describes two people united in mind and body or functioning as one. 'Alter egos' means alternative selves or personae and does not express their mutual unity.
罪はない here means Kiri is not at fault or is innocent. 'Has no sin' imposes an unnatural religious formulation.

rows.jp: けど俺は……俺の怪物は、身じろぎしてしまった。

ghs.en: but I... my monster was already stirring.

rows.en: I put an arm around her back.

ghs.assessment: The first-person narrator says he puts an arm or his hands around her back. The English removes him as agent and describes unidentified hands moving on her.

rows.jp: 激情が索敵を甘くして、霧は気づかない。
rows.en: Her grief had blunted her vigilance. She did not notice.

ghs.en: Violent emotions make enemy warning mechanisms less sharp, and Kiri does not notice.

rows.jp: 少しずつ、情緒は沈静化していく。
rows.en: Little by little, her emotions settled.

ghs.en: Little by little, her emotions were transforming into calmness.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says her emotions gradually settle down. The English changes the state into a transformation toward an abstract noun and unnecessarily shifts into past progressive.

rows.jp: その頃には、俺はすっかり霧を抱きしめていた。
rows.en: By then, I was holding Kiri in a full embrace.

ghs.en: By then, I had completely hugged Kiri.
ghs.assessment: すっかり here means that by then he was fully holding her in an embrace. 'Completely hugged' incorrectly modifies the completed act by degree.
The dialogue opens with a double quotation mark but closes with a single quotation mark.
The surname-plus-status address is left in Japanese morphology rather than represented in English.

ghs.en: Taichi: "I am empty. So very much."

rows.jp: 見下ろせば小さな面差し。
rows.en: I looked down at her small face.

ghs.en: If I look down those small features of hers,
ghs.assessment: The Japanese is a descriptive fragment centered on the small face below him. The English creates an unfinished conditional and lacks the required preposition 'at' after 'look down.'

highlights.text: If I look down those small features of hers,

rows.jp: 深みをたたえた黒曜石がふたつ、表面を薄い塩水で濡らす。
rows.en: Two pieces of obsidian, deep and dark, their surfaces filmed with salt water.

ghs.en: I can see a pair of obsidian stones, full with sadness to the depths, moistening her face with thin salty water.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese likens her two deep eyes to obsidian and says a thin layer of salt water wets their surfaces. The English adds sadness, then makes the stones actively moisten her whole face, reversing what is wetting what.

highlights.text: I can see a pair of obsidian stones, full with sadness to the depths, moistening her face with thin salty water.

rows.jp: 「豊は幸せだったと思うよ。霧もいたし、イヤなことは忘れてたし」
rows.en: “I think Yutaka was happy. He had you, and he’d forgotten the bad things.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I think Yutaka was happy, you know. Because you were there too, Kiri, so he could forget about the bad things."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese lists Kiri's presence and his having forgotten unpleasant things as parallel reasons. The English makes her presence the cause that enabled his forgetting.

highlights.text: Because you were there too, Kiri, so he could forget about the bad things.

rows.jp: 「最期まで、幸せだったって、俺は思ってる」
rows.en: “I think he was happy right up to the end.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "He was happy until his last, that's what I believe."
ghs.assessment: 最期まで means until the end or his final moment. 'Until his last' requires a following noun in English.
The narrator brings his own face closer to Kiri. The English makes him move her face instead.

rows.jp: 顔を交差するように重ねて。
rows.en: I angled my face over hers.
And took a kiss from her.
I tightened my arms around her.

ghs.assessment: 強く抱きしめた means held or embraced her tightly. 'Hugged with strength' is not idiomatic English.
霧の息が詰まった says Kiri's breath caught or stopped. The English instead says her ongoing breathing became difficult and also omits the possessive apostrophe.

rows.jp: フェンスに押しつけて、唇を吸い続ける。
rows.en: I pinned her against the fence and kept sucking at her lips.

ghs.en: Pushing her against the fence, I continue to suck her lips.
ghs.assessment: In this context 唇を吸う describes continuing the kiss. 'Suck her lips' is distractingly anatomical and nonidiomatic in English.

rows.jp: 驚きが、霧の思考力を奪っていた。
rows.en: Shock had robbed Kiri of the ability to think.

ghs.en: The surprise had stripped Kiri of the ability to think.

rows.en: Shock left her barely able to resist.

ghs.assessment: わからない here is 'I don't know' in answer to whether she is lonely. 'Don't get it' instead suggests failure to understand the question.

rows.jp: 今度は歯茎の内側に、侵略していく。
rows.en: This time, I invaded the space behind her teeth.

ghs.en: This time I go invade the inside of the teethridge.
ghs.assessment: 歯茎 means the gums. 'Teethridge' is not the standard anatomical term and is presented as a closed compound not recognized in English.

rows.jp: 同時に手を、スカートの中に。
rows.en: At the same time, I put a hand under her skirt.

ghs.en: And at the same time, my hands go inside her skirt.

rows.jp: 突如として抵抗が強まる。
俺は薄笑いを浮かべていたんだと思う。きっと。
rows.en: I think I was smirking. I must have been.

ghs.en: I think I am making a faint smile. Definitely.
ghs.assessment: The narrator retrospectively thinks he must have been wearing a faint smile. The English switches to present progressive and sets tentative 'I think' against an independent assertion of certainty.

highlights.text: I think I am making a faint smile. Definitely.

rows.jp: 衝撃が、ゆっくりと嫌悪に覆われていく様を、俺は見ていた。
rows.en: I watched her shock slowly give way to disgust.

ghs.en: I could see how the the shock was slowing being covered up by disgust.
ghs.assessment: The article is duplicated, and the adverb modifying 'being covered' must be 'slowly,' not 'slowing.'
The Japanese says she passes by Taichi's side. 'Underarm' names the armpit or a throwing style and lacks the possessive needed even for a literal body reference.

rows.en: A creaking door. A closing door.

ghs.assessment: The source presents two beats: the door creaks, then the door closes. The English omits the closing beat entirely.

rows.en: I covered my face with one hand.

ghs.en: I cover my face with my hands.

rows.jp: なるほど確かにこれはマズイ。
rows.en: I see. Yes, this was bad.

ghs.en: I see, it's certain, this is very bad.
ghs.assessment: なるほど確かに means roughly 'I see—this really is bad.' The English strings two discourse markers and two finite clauses together with commas.

highlights.text: I see, it's certain, this is very bad.

rows.jp: 口元が酷薄そうに吊り上がっていた。
rows.en: The corners of my mouth had curled into a cruel smile.

ghs.en: The edges of my mouth lifted in apparent inhuman cruelty.
I ended up estranged from Kiri.

rows.jp: 部活にもあまり顔を出さなくなった。
rows.en: She rarely showed her face at the club anymore.

ghs.en: She nearly stopped showing face at club.
ghs.assessment: The idiom is 'show her face,' and the club requires a determiner in this construction.

rows.jp: 美希が強引に連れてくることはあったが、俺のことは避けた。
rows.en: Miki sometimes dragged her there, but she avoided me.

ghs.en: There were times when Miki would forcibly bring her along, but she avoided me.

rows.jp: 会話もなくなり、関係は途絶した。
rows.en: We stopped speaking, and the relationship was severed.

rows.jp: そんなことが、あったんだ―――

ghs.en: And that... was one of the things that did happen---
